item.name: Authentication
item.description:
### 1\. Register

**Method:** **POST**

**URL:**

```
{{base_url}}/api/accounts/register/

 ```

**Body → raw → JSON:**

```
{
    "username": "postmanuser",
    "email": "postman@example.com",
    "password": "Test@12345"
}

 ```

No Authorization header is needed.

---

### 2\. Login

**Method:** **POST**

**URL:**

```
{{base_url}}/api/accounts/login/

 ```

**Body → raw → JSON:**

```
{
    "username": "postmanuser",
    "password": "Test@12345"
}

 ```

Again, no Authorization header.

```
{
    "access": "eyJ...",
    "refresh": "eyJ..."
}

 ```

For now, **copy the** **`access`** **token**.

Go to:

**ShopHub API → Variables**

and put the access token into:

``` python
const data = pm.response.json();

if (data.access) {
    pm.collectionVariables.set("access_token", data.access);
}

if (data.refresh) {
    pm.collectionVariables.set("refresh_token", data.refresh);
}

 ```

---

### 3\. Get Profile

**Method:** `GET`

**URL:**

```
{{base_url}}/api/accounts/profile/

 ```

Authorization:

**Authorization tab → Bearer Token**

Token:

```
{{access_token}}

 ```

```
Authorization: Bearer <your-token>

 ```

You should get the authenticated user's profile.

---

### 4\. Refresh Token

**Method:** `POST`

**URL:**

```
{{base_url}}/api/token/refresh/

 ```

Body → raw → JSON:

```
{
    "refresh": "YOUR_REFRESH_TOKEN"
}

 ```

item.name: Products
item.description:
StartFragment

### 1\. List Products

**GET**

```
{{base_url}}/api/products/

 ```

Authorization:

```
Bearer {{access_token}}

 ```

Test this first.

---

### 2\. Product Detail

**GET**

```
{{base_url}}/api/products/1/

 ```

Replace `1` with an existing product ID.

Authorization:

```
Bearer {{access_token}}

 ```

---

### 3\. Create Product

Because your serializer uses:

```
fields = '__all__'

 ```

the important writable fields are:

```
name
description
price
stock
brand
category
image
is_active

 ```

`id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are generated by Django, so **don't send those**.

For Postman:

**POST**

```
{{base_url}}/api/products/create/

 ```

Authorization:

```
Bearer {{access_token}}

 ```

For the body, use:

**Body → form-data**

| Key | Value | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | iPhone 16 | Text |
| `description` | Apple iPhone 16 smartphone | Text |
| `price` | 79999.00 | Text |
| `stock` | 10 | Text |
| `brand` | Apple | Text |
| `category` | 1 | Text |
| `is_active` | true | Text |

For `image`, add:

```
Key: image
Type: File

 ```

item.name: Addresses
item.description:
StartFragment

### 1\. List Addresses

**GET**

```
{{base_url}}/api/addresses/

 ```

Authorization:

```
Bearer {{access_token}}

 ```

---

### 2\. Create Address

**POST**

```
{{base_url}}/api/addresses/

 ```

Authorization:

```
Bearer {{access_token}}

 ```

Use **Body → raw → JSON**:

```
{
    "full_name": "Jaswanth Roy",
    "phone_number": "9876543210",
    "address_line_1": "Main Road",
    "address_line_2": "Near Temple",
    "street": "Main Street",
    "village": "Kotha Vellampalli",
    "city": "Piduguralla",
    "district": "Palnadu",
    "state": "Andhra Pradesh",
    "pincode": "522xxx",
    "country": "India",
    "landmark": "Near Temple"
}

 ```

Don't send:

```
id
user
is_default
created_at
updated_at

 ```

---

### 3\. Address Detail

**GET**

```
{{base_url}}/api/addresses/1/

 ```

Replace `1` with the actual address ID.

Authorization:

```
Bearer {{access_token}}

 ```

You can also create separate `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` requests against the same URL because your `AddressDetailAPIView` supports all three:

```
PUT    {{base_url}}/api/addresses/1/
PATCH  {{base_url}}/api/addresses/1/
DELETE {{base_url}}/api/addresses/1/

 ```

### 4\. Set Default Address

**POST**

```
{{base_url}}/api/addresses/1/default/

 ```

Authorization:

```
Bearer {{access_token}}

 ```

No body required.

item.name: Payments
item.description:
### Verify Payment

**Method:** `POST`

**URL:**

```
{{base_url}}/api/payments/verify/

 ```

**Authorization → Bearer Token:**

```
{{access_token}}

 ```

**Body → raw → JSON:**

```
{
    "razorpay_order_id": "order_xxxxxxxxxx",
    "razorpay_payment_id": "pay_xxxxxxxxxx",
    "razorpay_signature": "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
}

 ```

Use the **actual values returned by Razorpay** when you test it. Don't put fake values and expect verification to succeed.
